transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We know folks are coming from across security, cloud and legal so I appreciate the bandwidth. Quick intros?
[00:12] Rachel (Novus CISO): Rachel Kim here, CISO at Novus. We're primarily focused on EU customer data residency and ensuring no cross-border processing without a clear lawful basis.
[00:20] Martin (Novus Head Cloud): Martin Lopez, head of cloud engineering. I'll own the technical constraints - regions, VPCs, networking.
[00:26] Lisa (Novus Legal): Lisa Chen, privacy counsel. I'll flag contractual requirements and retention.
[00:31] Alex: Great. From Redwood, I'm Alex Monroe, and Priya Shah is our SE, Jordan's joining on the engineering side.
[00:38] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all. We'll mostly cover how region pinning works and the guarantees we can commit to.
[00:45] [00:46] Alex: Agenda for today — quick product recap, deep-dive on data residency/region pinning, encryption/KMS and audit logs, discuss sub-processors, and agree next steps. Sound good?
[00:53] Rachel: Yes. We have a fairly short list of must-haves: EU-only processing for EU customers, auditable logs, customer-managed keys ideally, and a clear list of any subcontractors.
[01:05] Priya: Understood. We'll start with region pinning. At a high level Redwood supports explicit region pinning per-tenant or per-route; that means requests for pinned routes are routed and executed in the selected region — e.g., eu-west-1 — and we avoid cross-region fallbacks unless you enable them.
[01:22] Martin: When you say "avoid cross-region fallbacks" what are the failure modes? If eu capacity is full do you queue or fail?
[01:30] Priya: By default we won't spill over to another region. We have configurable policies: hard pin (reject/fail if unavailable), soft pin (queue for X seconds), and fallback rules (only to GRAY-certified compatible variants in same legal region). For Novus we recommend hard pin for regulated EU tenants.
[01:48] Rachel: Hard pin is preferable. Our regulators are strict about processing location.
[01:52] [02:00] Alex: Quick note — we can also expose metrics for pinned-route rejects and queue times to the Redwood Console so you get visibility.
[02:07] Samir (Platform Architect): How is data routed at the network level? Are we sending any tokens or payloads to a control plane in the US?
[02:15] Jordan (Redwood SE): Good question. Control plane metadata (non-customer content) may be managed from Redwood's control plane which can be in the US, but payloads for pinned routes are kept in-region for inference and storage. We can provide a control-plane/data-plane separation doc. There are low-sensitivity metadata calls that may cross borders, but we provide options to minimize that.
[02:35] Martin: We need a clear diagram showing which API calls hit the control plane and which stay in-region.
[02:40] Priya: We'll attach a diagram.
[02:42] [03:00] Lisa: About sub-processors — who are you using today? Any cloud providers or third parties that might process payloads for EU tenants?
[03:08] Alex: Our primary infra providers are major cloud hyperscalers; we use region-specific compute (e.g., GCP eu-west-1 or AWS eu-west-1). Sub-processors list includes cloud providers, metrics provider, and a small set of managed services. We'll share the up-to-date sub-processor list and MSAs.
[03:25] Lisa: We need contractual commitments (DPA) and the list with locations and data processing purposes.
[03:30] Alex: We'll send the DPA template and sub-processor CSV.
[03:34] [04:00] Rachel: KMS — we prefer customer-managed keys where possible. Can Redwood support a Novus-owned KMS key (BYOK) for encryption at rest and in transit?
[04:12] Priya: We support KMS integrations. For hosted customers we can integrate with customer-managed keys (e.g., AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault) for encryption at rest in the data plane. There are some limitations around model weights caching that we should call out — ephemeral caches may be encrypted with our service keys but customer data stored in long-term storage can use your keys.
[04:34] Martin: Can we bring our own key that never leaves our control plane? We need to rotate keys on our schedule.
[04:42] Priya: Yes, we support key rotation cycles and can expose rotation APIs. For BYOK, we negotiate a configuration where the customer key encrypts persistent storage blobs; transient in-memory operations still use hardware boundaries but not the customer KMS directly for every token due to latency. We'll document exact flows.
[05:02] [05:30] Alex: On the auditability side — logs, retention, and export. We can stream audit logs to customer-owned log sinks (e.g., S3, Cloud Storage, or SIEM) in the pinned region. We also retain internal logs for X days by default with options for extended retention (add-on).
[05:45] Rachel: Important that logs include request IDs, route, region, and whether data left region or was processed solely in-region. Also need cryptographic verification or signed attestations?
[05:56] Priya: We can surface signed attestations for deployments and timestamps, and include requestID/route/region in the logs. For higher assurance we have an option to deliver periodic signed manifests of processing locations.
[06:12] Lisa: What about GDPR data subject requests — if an EU subject requests deletion, can you ensure all copies (caches, backups, audit logs) are removed?
[06:22] Jordan: We have deletion workflows tied to routing keys. For persistent storage we can delete and then provide a certificate of deletion. Backups and backups retention policies depend on the configured retention; we'll show where snapshots live and processes for deletion.
[06:38] [07:00] Martin: Are any ML providers or model vendors considered sub-processors? For example, if you use an external hosted model for some tasks, does data leave our tenant region?
[07:10] Alex: We vet model vendors. For Novus we can limit models to those we host in-region or provide a local variant. We avoid calling external hosted models outside the pinned region for pinned tenants. Any external model vendor usage will be declared in the sub-processor list along with location.
[07:26] Rachel: Cross-border lawful basis — if we have EU customers, we want processing to remain EU-only unless there's an explicit contractual or legal basis. How does Redwood document that?
[07:36] Priya: We can include region-only processing clauses in the DPA and provide a technical attestation. For data transfers for troubleshooting we require double opt-in and will anonymize data where appropriate.
[07:50] [08:15] Samir: For troubleshooting, will support engineers ever ask for a data extract? If so, where does that data land?
[08:22] Alex: We have a policy: PII/extracted customer content is only provided after customer approval and redaction requirements. For EU customers, we prefer session recordings that are scrubbed. We can provide temporary access to a copy hosted in the EU for triage.
[08:38] Lisa: We'll want those processes documented and included in the DPA.
[08:42] [09:00] Priya: A quick note on SSO and RBAC — we integrate with SAML/SSO providers and support SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC can be configured to limit who can change region pinning configs and who can access logs.
[09:16] Rachel: Good. We'll require admin-level separation; only a small set of Novus admins can change pinning.
[09:22] Priya: Role-based permissions exist at the org and route level; we'll show the admin roles and audit trail.
[09:30] [10:00] Martin: Performance impact: does hard pinning into EU increase latency compared to a global fallthrough? We need to understand tradeoffs for SLAs.
[10:09] Jordan: There's a small delta depending on where the user is located; for EU customers served from eu-west, latency is comparable to other EU-hosted services. The larger concern is capacity management — hard pin can lead to rejects if capacity is saturated, which is why we recommend planned reserved capacity (Dedicated) for production-critical EU traffic.
[10:32] Alex: We can provide performance benchmarks by region and projected token throughput for your expected QPS as part of the pilot.
[10:40] [11:00] Rachel: Are you willing to include a clause in the SLA about region enforcement — e.g., if data is processed outside of region due to Redwood's error there are remedies?
[11:10] Alex: Yes, we can discuss contractual remedies in the Enterprise DPA/SLA. We'll escalate that to legal to draft appropriate language.
[11:18] Lisa: And audit rights — can we run an annual audit or get a third-party attestation on the controls?
[11:25] Alex: We have SOC 2 Type II reports and ISO summaries. For deeper audits, we can support a review and coordinate with our security team. There may be scoping and reasonable notice requirements.
[11:36] [12:00] Priya: On sub-processor updates — we publish a rolling list and notify customers in advance of substantive changes. For high-risk sub-processors we require opt-in or contractual notice.
[12:15] Rachel: Notification windows? 30/60/90 days?
[12:18] Alex: Standard is 30 days for non-critical, 60 days for critical — but negotiable for enterprise agreements.
[12:26] [13:00] Martin: Technical ask — show us a sample region pin config and how it's enforced in the API or via console.
[13:06] Priya: We'll include an example config snippet and a short video of configuring a routed rule and pinned model assignment.
[13:14] [13:30] Lisa: Data retention — default logs retention vs. longer-term archives. We need retention windows to match our policy: e.g., event logs 90 days, full request bodies up to 30 days unless flagged for compliance reasons. Can that be customized per-tenant?
[13:46] Jordan: Yes, retention is configurable per-tenant with tiered options. Backups and cold storage have different SLA windows and are subject to add-on pricing.
[13:56] [14:30] Alex: A few risk items to flag: 1) ephemeral caches — these are in-memory and flushed based on TTL; 2) model telemetry may capture prompts for training unless opted out; 3) control plane metadata. We'll document how to opt-out of telemetry and ensure training data exclusions.
[14:50] Rachel: We will require opt-out and contractual assurances that customer prompts are not used for model training.
[14:57] Alex: Agreed — the enterprise agreement can include a no-training clause for Novus data.
[15:05] [15:30] Priya: Operationally, for pilot we'll propose: set up EU-only org in our EU region, configure hard pining for sample routes, provision a customer-managed KMS key for storage, and stream audit logs to your EU S3 bucket. Then run a small benchmark and verify logs/attestations.
[15:48] Martin: Sounds good. What about monitoring — token-level cost and latency?
[15:52] Alex: All visible in Redwood Console — and we can export dashboards or integrate with your telemetry.
[16:00] [16:30] Lisa: Any known sub-processors outside EU that might have incidental access?
[16:36] Alex: Most sub-processors are region-scoped. We will mark any global services and provide details.
[16:42] [17:00] Rachel: I want a one-page summary we can show the board that says: EU data stays in EU, control plane flows, KMS BYOK support, auditability, and next steps.
[17:13] Alex: We'll draft that one-pager and include a technical appendix.
[17:18] [18:00] Priya: I'll add screenshots and the config snippet.
[18:03] Alex: OK, last section — edge cases. What if a legal hold requires data replication outside EU?
[18:12] Lisa: We need a legal escape clause but with explicit approvals and logging.
[18:16] Priya: We can implement an "admin-approved transfer" workflow that timestamps and records the reason, approver and what changed.
[18:26] [19:00] Martin: Are there metrics for how often fallback/spillover has happened historically?
[19:08] Jordan: We can provide historical telemetry on spillover events per region for comparable customers, redacted of course.
[19:14] Rachel: That will help risk evaluation.
[19:18] [20:00] Alex: To recap: Redwood will share SOC 2 and ISO materials, sub-processor list and DPA draft, region pinning architecture diagram and config examples, and a one-pager for execs. Novus will provide region requirements, retention policy, and confirm who will be the admins. We'll target pilot kickoff week of 2025-07-28.
[20:38] Lisa: Agreed. Also legal will review the DPA once received.
[20:42] Alex: Great. Any other questions?
[20:46] Samir: None here.
[20:48] Rachel: No, thanks.
[20:50] Alex: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the materials and meeting notes.
[20:56] [21:00] End of transcript (automated Fireflies note: transcript may contain transcription imperfections such as mis-attributed speakers or minor word errors).
